P001.text: Act on a prospective cohort of newly created accounts, treating onboarding trajectories as a mixture of potentially distinguishable behaviors.

P002.text: Confusing setup, missing team information and waiting for a roster cycle are hypotheses suggested by eight interviews, not established segments or prevalence estimates.

P003.text: Assume accounts may repeatedly alternate between active product work and preparation or waiting; test that assumption rather than assigning each account a fixed cause.

P004.text: Use the same onboarding pathway and observation conditions across the initial cohort.

P005.text: Define the moving-phase counterpart as active work through invitations, draft saves and publication; define the stationary-phase counterpart as relatively persistent setup requirements and readiness constraints that can retain accounts before further progress.

P006.text: At successive milestones and a consistently timed inactivity follow-up, combine existing events with brief questions about the next required action, information availability, offline preparation and intended roster date.

P007.text: Record repeated progress–waiting–return transitions, allowing multiple or unknown reasons.

P008.text: Follow accounts through their stated next roster opportunity plus a predeclared grace period; use a fixed maximum follow-up for unknown dates and mark unfinished trajectories as censored.

P009.text: Before reviewing results, set minimum evidence and practically worthwhile improvement thresholds.

P010.text: Use the single small release slot for the smallest change addressing a recurrent, independently corroborated, product-addressable retention point: clearer instructions for verified comprehension problems, information collection support for verified preparation problems, or a timed return aid for verified postponement.

P011.text: If evidence does not distinguish an actionable constraint, use the slot for missing measurement instead.

P012.text: Where feasible, randomly assign eligible accounts to the selected change or the existing experience, keeping measurement identical.

P013.text: Stop recruitment and analysis at predeclared sample and follow-up limits; stop exposure early only under predefined harm criteria.

P014.text: Look for separated concentrations of trajectories in milestone position, time spent waiting, number of returns to active work and time to first publication.

P015.text: For example, renewed progress after obtaining team information or publication near a previously stated roster date would be candidate signals, not assumed observations.

P016.text: Report accounts with no return and incomplete follow-up alongside published accounts.

P017.text: In the release comparison, observe first-publication rates within a common window, time to publication, retention at the targeted checkpoint and predefined guardrails such as publication errors.

P018.text: Reproducible differences under common conditions would support distinguishable onboarding behaviors and characterize their relative retention at requirements or readiness constraints.

P019.text: Agreement between event patterns and contemporaneous preparation reports would strengthen a proposed mechanism.

P020.text: A sufficiently precise randomized improvement in first publication would support a causal effect of the tested change for the studied accounts and window; reduced delay at the targeted checkpoint would additionally support, but not establish, the proposed mechanism.

P021.text: Roll out only if the predeclared benefit and guardrail criteria are met.

P022.text: Otherwise retain the existing experience and use the uncertainty or conflicting evidence to specify the next targeted observation or test.

P023.text: Different causes can produce the same inactivity or publication timing, analogous to co-elution; one account can also experience several causes.

P024.text: Milestone events are nonspecific detectors, and absent events cannot distinguish abandonment from offline preparation.

P025.text: Added questions may change behavior, and self-reports may be incomplete.

P026.text: Roster timing, team size, acquisition mix and changes in onboarding conditions can shift apparent retention, so record these conditions and compare like observation windows.

P027.text: Behavioral retention alone does not identify a cause: seek corroboration through preparation reports, task observation or a controlled intervention.

P028.text: A small sample, sparse publications or censored accounts may leave effects unresolved; failure to meet the evidence threshold is not proof of no benefit.

P029.text: Without randomization, describe release differences as associations subject to confounding.
